title: Trace annotator cheatsheet and widget prioritization
content:
Purpose
This is a compact, operator-friendly cheatsheet for annotating traces and prioritizing dashboard widgets during the upcoming rollout of the compact observability surface for inference. The doc is intentionally short — a single-page reference operators can paste into incident channels and a companion checklist for dashboard owners.

Scope and audience
- Audience: oncall operators, SREs, runtime engineers, and dashboard owners who need a fast mapping from symptom -> trace annotation -> dashboard action.
- Scope: inference request path (API gateway -> router -> runtime shard -> model exec -> cache layer -> response aggregator). Excludes offline batch jobs and embeddings ingestion pipelines (we'll link those separately).

High-level goals
1) Standardize span names and a minimal attribute set so sessions/requests can be reconstituted quickly.
2) Define a compact metric set and widget priority tiers so dashboards remain small and effective for paging.
3) Provide a small checklist for annotating rollouts / experiment traces to support postmortems and performance regressions.

Span naming conventions (recommended)
- api.request.received  -- first inbound HTTP entry for a user request (include request_id, route, tenant_id)
- api.request.auth     -- auth/quota check (outcome: allowed/denied)
- router.route.resolve -- routing decision (chosen_model, chosen_variant, fallback_reason)
- runtime.exec.start   -- runtime scheduling and queue wait start (queue_len, priority)
- runtime.exec.invoke  -- actual model invocation (model, seq_len, kv_cache_hit)
- runtime.exec.kvfetch  -- KV/prefix cache fetch (cache_key, hit)
- runtime.exec.kvstore  -- cache write path (evicted, ttl)
- runtime.exec.kernel   -- low-level kernel/quant path (kernel_name, dtype, device)
- runtime.exec.finish   -- total runtime exec end (tokens_generated)
- response.aggregate    -- aggregation/streaming assembly and postproc (streaming:true/false)
- api.response.sent     -- final response send (status_code, latency_ms)

Required span attributes (minimal set)
- request_id (string) -- unique per API request
- session_id (string) -- optional but strongly recommended for chat/multi-turn flows
- tenant_id (string) -- customer identifier for multi-tenant correlation
- route (string) -- route name or endpoint
- model (string) -- model identifier + quantization tag (eg: gpt-j-6b.q4_0)
- variant (string) -- fallback or canary tag (eg: production, canary-2024-11)
- shard (string) -- runtime shard/host id
- seq_len (int) -- prompt sequence length in tokens
- kv_cache_hit (bool) -- whether prefix KV cache was used for this request
- kernel (string) -- kernel name or path selected for exec
- queue_wait_ms (int) -- time spent in runtime queue
- exec_ms (int) -- time spent in actual model execution

Sampling and retention notes
- Default sampling: 0.5% full-trace sample across all tenants for regular traffic; increase to 100% for tenants in active incident windows or canary rollouts (feature-flagged).
- Severity-weighted sampling: always keep traces where exec_ms > P99_latency_threshold OR error status_code != 200 OR kv_cache_hit=false on warm-cache flows.
- Redaction: redact prompt text; keep prompt token counts and prompt hashes when safe. Use privacy tags for PHI-sensitive tenants.

Widget prioritization rubric (for compact dashboard lanes)
Tier 0 (must-have for paging):
- Per-tenant 95th/99th latency for api.request.received -> api.response.sent (latency_ms P95/P99)
- Request rate (rps) 1m/5m
- Error rate (4xx/5xx) by route and model
- Runtime queue length and queue_wait_ms distribution
- Token generation rate and cost-per-token estimate

Tier 1 (operational diagnosis):
- KV cache hit ratio (global & per-shard)
- Exec_ms distribution by model variant
- Inflight requests by shard and priority class
- Fallback rate (when router chooses fallback variant)

Tier 2 (investigation / forensics):
- Per-route span flamegraph sampler (hot spans for slow requests)
- Kernel selection cardinality over time (surfacing regressions after deployments)
- Request session-reconstruction quickcard (links to stored trace ids)

Widget sizing guidance
- Only one P99 panel per dashboard lane; prefer P95 for routine ops. Reserve P99 for incident dashboards.
- Use sparklines for long-term trends, heatmaps for latency slices, and small tables for top-k models by cost.

Trace annotation templates (copy-paste for rollout channels)
- Canary start: ANNOTATE request_id={{id}} tags=[canary,variant=canary-2024-11,experiment=kv-opt] note="canary start - watching queue and exec_ms"
- Canary failure: ANNOTATE request_id={{id}} tags=[canary,incident] note="canary observed >2x baseline P95 - escalate"
- Hotpath reproduction: ANNOTATE request_id={{id}} tags=[repro,hotpath] note="repro instructions: curl --header X-Req-Id={{id}} ..."

Rollout instrumentation checklist (pre-rollout)
- [ ] Add kernel and kv_cache attributes to spans in PR (GH: redwood/telemetry#482)
- [ ] Add lightweight synthetic probe that exercises canary model path
- [ ] Ensure dashboard Tier 0 panels exist and alerting thresholds are set for P95
- [ ] Configure increased trace sampling for canary tenant(s)
- [ ] Run smoke probe for 24h and validate metric drift < 5%

Quick operator drills (how to use this cheatsheet)
1) If latency alert fires: check Tier 0 P95 latency + queue length. If queue high, annotate run with "queue_backpressure" and escalate to runtime-scheduling.
2) If error spike: filter traces for status_code != 200, look for auth/route faults first (api.request.auth).
3) If model exec slow: examine kernel selection heatmap and exec_ms distribution by model. Tag traces and open OBS-311 with sample traces.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- How to surface kernel-level stalls without exploding trace cardinality? Proposal: aggregate per-minute kernel metrics (counts + 95th exec_ms) and only sample full traces when kernel-specific P95 jumps > 2x.
- Should we store prompt hashes centrally for easier repro? Privacy/legal wants stricter rules; need product/legal signoff for retention.

Next steps
- Iterate this cheatsheet into a single-pane Slack quicklink for oncall (owner: Dana Kim).
- Add small templated panels to dashboard starter kit and bump Tier 0 coverage for high-traffic tenants (owner: Aisha Patel).
- Review sampling and retention policy with privacy and legal (owner: Maya Singh).

Notes & references
- See linked Confluence page for full trace schema and attribute types.
- Related GH issue for kernel attributes: redwood/telemetry#482.
- Triage playbook references: OBS-311 (alerting thresholds and postmortem template).

Quick paste list (for runbooks)
- Key spans: api.request.received, runtime.exec.invoke, runtime.exec.finish, api.response.sent
- Key attrs: request_id, tenant_id, model, variant, shard, seq_len, kv_cache_hit, exec_ms

End of cheatsheet — keep this in incident runbook and sync with dashboard owners before each major runtime rollout.
